manifest.name: POS Self Order Stripe
manifest.summary: Addon for the Self Order App that allows customers to pay by Stripe.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Point of Sale Payment Methods (Stripe self-order/kiosk bridge)

security.note: no module-owned access rules/groups; reuses point_of_sale POS groups and the pos_self_order public gate (_verify_authorization). Routes declared website=True. Parent stripe_connection_token/payment_intent/capture require point_of_sale.group_pos_user, satisfied via the self_ordering_default_user_id the gate impersonates.

views.note: 1 data file views/assets_stripe.xml: a template inheriting pos_self_order.index that injects <script src='https://js.stripe.com/terminal/v1/'> into <head> (cannot be loaded via __manifest__ assets because the URL has no .js suffix). No backend form/list views.

behavioral_notes.observation: The bridge adds no fields and wires Stripe into the kiosk via two pos.payment.method overrides. _payment_request_from_kiosk overrides pos_self_order's no-op hook: it returns super() unless self.use_payment_terminal == 'stripe', otherwise it simply calls the parent module's self.stripe_payment_intent(order.amount_total) -- which creates a Stripe PaymentIntent with payment_method_types[]='card_present' and capture_method='manual' (terminal/card-present, manual capture) and returns the intent (including its client_secret) to the caller (/kiosk/payment). Unlike the Pine Labs/Razorpay siblings it builds no reference dict and starts no poll -- the Stripe Terminal SDK drives the reader client-side, so the server only mints the intent here. _load_pos_self_data_domain (@api.model) OR-extends pos_self_order's data-load domain so that, when config.self_ordering_mode == 'kiosk', the Stripe methods on config.payment_method_ids are shipped to the public kiosk OWL client (otherwise excluded by the base [('id','=',False)] domain). This terminal-enabling config switch is invisible to field metadata.

Stripe needs two server tokens before the reader can charge, both served public. (1) The payment trigger is pos_self_order's own /kiosk/payment/<pos_config_id>/kiosk (jsonrpc), to which the JS Stripe.startPayment posts the serialized order; that base route runs process_order (creating the pos.order in the open pos.session via sync_from_ui), then payment_method_sudo._payment_request_from_kiosk(order_sudo) -> stripe_payment_intent, returning {'order': _load_pos_self_data_read(...), 'payment_status': intent} so the client gets payment_status.client_secret. (2) /pos-self-order/stripe-connection-token/ (this module, public jsonrpc website=True) verifies the config via _verify_authorization(access_token,'',{}) and returns payment_method.stripe_connection_token() -- the parent's POST to Stripe terminal/connection_tokens, whose .secret the Stripe Terminal JS SDK consumes (onFetchConnectionToken) to authenticate the reader. The reader is then discovered/connected client-side by stripe_serial_number. This dual-token handshake is pure code, not metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: controllers/orders.py: PosSelfOrderControllerStripe.stripe_capture_payment -> stripe_capture_payment + amount check -> order.add_payment / action_pos_order_paid / _send_payment_result
behavioral_notes.observation: /pos-self-order/stripe-capture-payment/ (public jsonrpc website=True) is the settlement route -- there is NO polling. It verifies the config (_verify_authorization), calls pos.payment.method.stripe_capture_payment(payment_intent_id) (parent POST payment_intents/<id>/capture), and finds the pos.order by (access_token=order_access_token, config_id) (Unauthorized if missing). It then re-validates the captured amount server-side: float_is_zero(payment_method._stripe_calculate_amount(order.amount_total) - stripe_confirmation['amount'], precision_rounding=currency.rounding) AND stripe_confirmation['status'] == 'succeeded'. Only then does it write a pos.payment via order.add_payment({amount: order.amount_total, payment_date: now, payment_method_id, transaction_id=stripe_confirmation['id'], payment_status='succeeded', ...}), call order.action_pos_order_paid(), and -- if self_ordering_mode == 'kiosk' -- order._send_payment_result('Success') (config._notify('PAYMENT_STATUS') + receipt + kitchen order). If the amount mismatches or status != succeeded it order._send_payment_result('fail'). This server-side amount-equality guard against a client-supplied payment_intent_id is the key integrity behavior and is invisible to metadata. (Tests/test_self_order_kiosk_stripe.py mocks stripe_capture_payment and asserts the order reaches state 'paid'.)

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL self-order kiosk Stripe Terminal SDK handler + injected <script>) -- gap #3
behavioral_notes.observation: The client side is plain JS on the pos_self_order public OWL app (3 JS files, 0 OWL components; bundles pos_self_order.assets + pos_self_order.assets_tests): a non-OWL Stripe class (static/src/app/stripe.js) wrapping the global Stripe Terminal SDK, plus patches of PaymentPage.prototype (static/src/app/pages/payment_page/payment_page.js) and SelfOrder.prototype (static/src/app/services/self_order_service.js). The SDK itself is loaded by views/assets_stripe.xml injecting <script src='https://js.stripe.com/terminal/v1/'> into the self-order index <head>. PaymentPage.startPayment delegates to selfOrder.stripe.startPayment when use_payment_terminal === 'stripe'; SelfOrder.setup instantiates Stripe and tracks stripeState via handleReaderConnection. Stripe.startPayment: POST /kiosk/payment -> get client_secret + savedOrder -> connectReader() (StripeTerminal.create with onFetchConnectionToken -> /pos-self-order/stripe-connection-token; discoverReaders + connectReader matching stripe_serial_number) -> collectPaymentMethod(clientSecret) -> terminal.processPayment -> capturePayment(intent.id, savedOrder) which calls /pos-self-order/stripe-capture-payment with the order's access_token. There is no polling loop -- the Stripe Terminal SDK is synchronous/event-driven and only the capture round-trip settles. A test tour (static/tests/tours) exercises the kiosk Stripe flow. None of this reader/SDK orchestration is reverse-engineerable from Python.

it_architecture.application: pos_self_order_stripe (thin auto-installed bridge: wires the Stripe Terminal reader -- from pos_stripe -- into the pos_self_order kiosk self-payment flow via a pos.payment.method override, a connection-token + a capture route, an injected Stripe Terminal SDK <script>, and OWL kiosk patches)
software_services: /pos-self-order/stripe-connection-token/ (public jsonrpc, website=True; return Stripe terminal connection_token secret for the SDK to authenticate the reader)
/pos-self-order/stripe-capture-payment/ (public jsonrpc, website=True; capture the PaymentIntent, amount-check, settle pos.payment, bus-notify Success/fail)
(reused from pos_self_order) /kiosk/payment/<pos_config_id>/kiosk -> _payment_request_from_kiosk -> stripe_payment_intent (mint the card_present/manual PaymentIntent + client_secret)
logical_data_erm: pos.payment.method -> pos.config (config_ids; kiosk configs whose payment_method_ids include the Stripe method)
pos.payment.method -> pos.payment (the tender written by order.add_payment, base POS model)
pos.order -> pos.session (order created in the open session by /kiosk/payment process_order, base pos_self_order)
information_flows: depends: pos_self_order (kiosk app, /kiosk/payment, _payment_request_from_kiosk hook, _send_payment_result bus, pos_self_order.index template) + pos_stripe (use_payment_terminal='stripe', stripe_serial_number, stripe_connection_token/payment_intent/capture, _stripe_calculate_amount, payment.provider 'stripe')
client->server: kiosk PaymentPage -> SelfOrder.stripe.startPayment -> /kiosk/payment/<config>/kiosk -> _payment_request_from_kiosk -> stripe_payment_intent -> client_secret
client->server: Stripe Terminal SDK onFetchConnectionToken -> /pos-self-order/stripe-connection-token/ -> stripe_connection_token (terminal/connection_tokens) -> reader authenticated
client-side: discoverReaders + connectReader(stripe_serial_number) -> collectPaymentMethod(client_secret) -> terminal.processPayment (no server poll)

settlement: capturePayment -> /pos-self-order/stripe-capture-payment/ -> stripe_capture_payment (payment_intents/<id>/capture) -> amount-equality + status=='succeeded' guard -> order.add_payment (pos.payment) -> action_pos_order_paid -> (kiosk) _send_payment_result('Success') -> config._notify('PAYMENT_STATUS') + receipt + kitchen order; mismatch -> _send_payment_result('fail')

indirect outbound: the actual HTTPS calls to the Stripe API (_get_stripe_payment_provider._send_api_request) live in pos_stripe / the payment engine, not in this bridge; the browser also talks directly to Stripe via the Terminal SDK
frontend_components: Stripe (plain JS Stripe Terminal SDK wrapper, static/src/app/stripe.js)
PaymentPage.prototype (patch; route stripe payments to Stripe.startPayment)
SelfOrder.prototype (patch; instantiate Stripe, track stripeState, StripeError notifications)
assets_stripe.xml (template patch; inject Stripe Terminal SDK <script> into pos_self_order.index)

capabilities: Accept Self-Service Kiosk Card-Present Payment via a Stripe Terminal Reader
Authenticate the Stripe Terminal Reader from the Kiosk (connection token)
Capture a Stripe PaymentIntent and Settle it into the Kiosk Order (pos.payment), with a server-side amount check
Expose the Stripe Payment Method to the Kiosk Self-Order Client (kiosk-mode only)
value_streams: Kiosk-self-pay-by-Stripe: diner confirms order at the kiosk -> /kiosk/payment creates the pos.order + mints a card_present/manual PaymentIntent -> the Stripe Terminal SDK fetches a connection token, connects the reader (by serial), collects + processes the card -> the kiosk captures the intent -> the server re-checks the amount, writes a pos.payment, marks the order paid, and (kiosk) emits a PAYMENT_STATUS bus message + receipt/kitchen order
information_concepts: pos.payment (base; tender line written on capture)
pos.config (base; kiosk config exposing the terminal)
payment.provider ('stripe'; supplies the API credentials, via pos_stripe)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; reuses point_of_sale POS groups -- the parent Stripe methods require group_pos_user, met via the self_ordering_default_user_id the public gate impersonates)
policies: _payment_request_from_kiosk only acts when use_payment_terminal == 'stripe' (else delegates to super)
PaymentIntent is card_present + manual capture; amount via _stripe_calculate_amount (currency-scaled, not a fixed factor)
Stripe methods are loaded to the public kiosk client only when self_ordering_mode == 'kiosk' (_load_pos_self_data_domain OR-extension)
capture settles a pos.payment ONLY if the captured amount equals _stripe_calculate_amount(order.amount_total) (float_is_zero) AND status == 'succeeded'; otherwise _send_payment_result('fail')
routes verify the config (_verify_authorization) and bind the order by access_token (Unauthorized otherwise); the reader is matched to the method by stripe_serial_number
stakeholders: Customer / diner (taps/inserts card on the Stripe Terminal reader at the kiosk)
Stripe Terminal reader + Stripe API (external payment device/provider, via pos_stripe + payment.provider 'stripe')
Restaurant / Store Manager (configures the Stripe method + reader serial on the kiosk pos.config)
Accountant (consumes the resulting pos.payment via the base POS session closing entry)
metrics: Stripe kiosk tender amounts roll up via base pos.payment / report.pos.order (no module-specific report)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: pos_self_order_stripe is a thin payment-terminal bridge inside the in-store self-service checkout: its sole act is collecting the customer's tender on a Stripe Terminal reader and completing a pos.payment on the kiosk pos.order so the order can be marked paid. That places it on the retail Sell/checkout primary activity of the value chain (Stabell & Fjeldstad chain / transform), inherited from its point_of_sale -> pos_self_order lineage, and maps to APQC 3.0 (Market and Sell Products and Services) because the operation it adds -- capturing payment to close the kiosk sale -- is part of selling/closing the counter transaction, not treasury/AR (APQC 9.0), realized downstream by the base POS session closing entry. It carries a 'network' overtone (it mediates between the diner, the Stripe Terminal reader and the Stripe API through public token/capture routes), but, like its pos_safaricom / pos_online_payment siblings, the value logic it actually completes is the chain sell transaction, so it is classified chain. (The host pos_self_order is itself classed 'network' as the mediating self-order channel; this child adds only a tender device to that channel's kiosk mode, so it is read with the underlying POS sell rather than the channel mediation.)

standard_capabilities: pay a self-service kiosk order with a Stripe Terminal reader (use_payment_terminal = 'stripe')
automatic kiosk order creation + card_present/manual PaymentIntent in one /kiosk/payment round-trip
Stripe Terminal JS SDK reader connection (connection token, discover/connect by serial) and client-side card collection
manual capture with a server-side amount-equality + 'succeeded' guard before writing the pos.payment
Stripe method auto-exposed to the kiosk client only in kiosk self-ordering mode; PAYMENT_STATUS bus Success/fail signal
typical_fits: fast-food / retail self-order kiosks with a Stripe Terminal card reader (any Stripe-supported region/currency)
a Stripe method + stripe_serial_number on the kiosk pos.config.payment_method_ids, backed by a published 'stripe' payment.provider
kiosk pay-each flow where the diner taps a card at the kiosk before the order goes to the kitchen
common_gaps: requires the Stripe Terminal SDK <script> to load (injected into the index) and a reachable Stripe API; offline kiosks cannot charge
reader must be discoverable and its serial must match stripe_serial_number on the method
no module-specific reconciliation/reporting beyond the base pos.payment line (refunds live in pos_stripe.stripe_refund, not exposed to the kiosk)
tip/over-capture (amount_to_capture) is not used from the kiosk path -- it captures the exact authorized amount
a published Stripe payment.provider for the company is required (_get_stripe_payment_provider raises otherwise)
drive_hints: curl jsonrpc /pos-self-order/stripe-connection-token with {'access_token':cfg.access_token,'payment_method_id':...} (returns the Stripe connection_token secret; needs a valid token + published stripe provider)
open a kiosk POS (self_ordering_mode='kiosk') with a Stripe method + reader serial and place an order to trigger PaymentPage.startPayment -> Stripe.startPayment
run the kiosk Stripe test tour: addons/pos_self_order_stripe/tests/test_self_order_kiosk_stripe.py (mocks capture, asserts order state 'paid')

open_questions: Exact OWL correlation: how the kiosk PaymentPage reacts to the PAYMENT_STATUS bus notification after the capture route already wrote the pos.payment (vs the synchronous capturePayment return).
Failure handling if terminal.processPayment succeeds client-side but /pos-self-order/stripe-capture-payment then fails the amount check (the customer's card may be authorized but not captured).
Whether a non-kiosk (mobile) self_ordering_mode ever reaches the Stripe capture path -- the success bus signal is gated on kiosk only.
Reader-sharing / fail_if_in_use behavior when two kiosks point at the same stripe_serial_number reader concurrently.
